sources.entry: Sniffnet - Application to comfortably monitor your network traffic. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/GyulyVGC/sniffnet) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Sniffnet is a cross-platform desktop application for monitoring your network traffic, with real-time charts, connection inspection, and geolocation of remote hosts.
summary.what_it_does: Sniffnet lets you pick a network adapter on your computer and inspect the traffic passing through it. It shows real-time charts of traffic intensity and overall statistics about your Internet traffic. Each connection can be searched and inspected live, and it identifies services and protocols (the README cites 6000+), plus which programs are using bandwidth. Hosts are enriched with geographic location, domain name, and ASN data (IP geolocation and ASN data are credited to MaxMind). Traffic captures can be imported and exported as PCAP files, custom IP blacklists can be loaded to flag dangerous connections, and notifications can be set for defined network events. The README also mentions a minimize mode that keeps monitoring running, and custom themes.
use_cases: monitor network traffic on my PC
inspect live network connections and remote hosts
find which programs are using bandwidth
export network captures as PCAP files
look up geolocation and ASN of remote hosts
how_to_run: Download a prebuilt installer for your platform (DEB, RPM, or AppImage for Linux; other installers via the README's download table or alternative installation methods)
Install the required dependencies for your operating system (see the README's required dependencies page)
If the interface shows rendering glitches, set ICED_BACKEND=tiny-skia to use the CPU-only renderer
notable: Cross-platform desktop app with prebuilt DEB, RPM, and AppImage packages across x64, arm64, x86, and armhf architectures
Identifies 6000+ upper layer services, protocols, trojans, and worms
Custom IP blacklists and notifications for defined network events
Custom themes and translations into 20+ languages
caveats: Requires installing extra system dependencies for packet capture on your operating system
Some graphics setups may show rendering bugs, requiring a switch to the tiny-skia renderer
The README says sponsorship supports development, and the project is described as free and open-source; no paid tier is mentioned
keywords: see what my computer is connecting to
